To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a new solution to Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton gravity and that the residual force in the interaction between charged dilaton black hole is non‐Newtonian.
we have found a family of multicentered solutions in arbitrary dimensions for the system consisting of a scalar and vector field in a gravitational field.

(i) a multicentered solution for a dilaton black hole is obtained in arbitrary dimension, which is the generalization of the Majumard‐Papapetru solution, and (ii) the residual force remains even in the low‐velocity limit in general cases, and the residual force vanishes in the case with N=4
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between two extreme dilaton black holes.
the interaction of two charged dilaton black hole in arbitrary dimensions.
the interaction between extreme charged dilaton holes in the low energy limit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the interaction between two extreme dilaton black holes is repulsive in the low‐velocity limit, but the velocity‐dependent force is attractive in the high‐velocity limit, except for a particular case with N=a ^{2}.
the dilaton field plays an important role for the force law in the low‐velocity regime, but not in the high‐velocity regime.
the dilaton does not play a crucial role in the interaction of two charged dilaton black hole systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dilaton field is essential to the existence of multicentered solution, which is a necessary condition for the existence of the residual force between extreme charged dilaton holes.
the dilaton field plays a crucial role in the low‐velocity interaction between charged dilaton black hole systems.
there exists the residual velocity‐ dependent force in the low‐ energy limit of the extreme charged dilaton‐ black‐ hole interaction, which is a generalization of the Coulomb force.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the residual force between two extreme dilaton black holes is not always attractive, but it depends on the number of extra dimensions.
the dilaton field can be a useful tool to construct a new class of static multicentered solution, which may provide a new platform to study the interaction between two extreme dilaton black holes.
the residual velocity‐dependence of the interaction force is a generic feature in the low‐velocity limit.
